I set this up as a grid: 10 edits, each applied across 10 parents. The parents differ in what sits on each edge: all-conv, all-skip, all-pool, chain-only and direct-edge-only cells, plus mixed cells.

Applying the same edit to every parent means its effect can be compared across parent conditions. That is where interactions should show up, for example:
- the 0→3 conv/skip edit depending on whether the 0→1→2→3 chain carries convs;
- removing edge 0 depending on whether node 1 feeds the output;
- the edge 5 edit depending on whether node 2 has any input.

Where an edit would not change a parent, I replaced that parent with a close variant so none of the 100 experiments is wasted.
